sections.title: Bio
sections.content: Rt. Rev. Francis Mboya Matui is a dedicated Anglican leader with many years of pastoral, administrative, and missionary experience.

sections.title: Educational Background
items: Bachelor of Divinity (BD) – St. Paul’s University (2007–2010)
Diploma in Theology – St. Andrew’s College of Theology & Development, Kabare (1993–1996)

sections.title: Ministerial & Pastoral Experience
items: Vicar of multiple parishes
Diocesan Administrative Secretary
Archdeacon
Cathedral Canon

sections.title: Key Achievements
items: Spearheaded the construction of several churches and schools
Participated in cross-cultural mission work in Tanzania, Ethiopia, and South Sudan
Played a key role in transforming UCCS/ADSE from a church department into a development-focused organization

sections.title: Family
sections.content: Bishop Matui is married to Margaret K. Mboya, and they are blessed with two children.

sections.title: Bio
sections.content: Dr. Abednego Alibiri Ongeso is a scholar, health specialist, and committed Christian leader who brings extensive academic and professional experience to the leadership of Anglican Missions Africa. His work in health sciences, research, and community service reflects a strong commitment to improving lives and strengthening communities

sections.title: Educational Background
items: PhD – Great Lakes University of Kisumu
MSc Nursing (Maternal & Neonatal Health) – Moi University
BSc Nursing – Moi University
Diploma in Project Management – Kenya Institute of Management

sections.title: Professional Life
sections.content: Assistant Professor at Aga Khan University – Nairobi.

sections.title: Professional Experience
items: Lecturer at University of Nairobi
Lecturer at Daystar University
Assistant Lecturer – Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology
Project Officer – Kenya Red Cross (North Rift)
Nursing Officer I – Kakamega County Hospital.

sections.title: Family
sections.content: Married to Stella Chepleting Kogo since 2008; blessed with three children.

mayabi.name: Rev. Canon Captain Richard W. Mayabi
mayabi.title: Executive Director, Missions Anglicanes Afrique (AMA)

sections.title: Bio
sections.content: Rev. Canon Captain Richard W. Mayabi is the Founder of Missions Anglicanes Afrique (Anglican Missions Africa – AMA). The mission agency seeks to nurture a healthy and sustainable Church in Africa and beyond through leadership development, mission mobilization, and church strengthening initiatives.

sections.title: Work Experience
items: 2019: Director in charge of Capacity Building and Leadership Development at the Council for Anglican Provinces of Africa (CAPA)
2009 – 2018: General Secretary of Church Army Africa
2004 – 2008: Pioneer Parish Priest for ACK St. Jerome and St. Thomas parishes in All Saints Cathedral Diocese
1995 – 2003: Pioneer missionary and church planter in Makueni–Machakos Diocese

sections.title: Educational Background
items: Master of Theology (MTh) in Urban World – International Christian College Glasgow / Aberdeen University
Master of Arts (MA) in Mission Studies – Africa International University (AIU), Nairobi
Post Graduate Diploma (PGD) in Christian Ministries – Africa International University (AIU), Nairobi
Higher Diploma (HDP) in Theology – Carlile College, Church Army Africa
Diploma in Theology – Mission Studies, Exeter University, UK
Diploma in Discipleship Training School (DTS) – Youth With A Mission (YWAM), University of the Nations

sections.title: Family
sections.content: He is married to The Rev. Captain Patience Wanzala, and together they are blessed with three children.

sections.title: Mission Commitment
sections.content: Committed to raising leaders and strengthening the mission of the Church in Africa.

ron.name: The Very Rev. Canon Dr. Ronald D. Allen
ron.title: Board Advisor & Custodian of Vision

sections.title: Bio
sections.content: The Very Rev. Canon Dr. Ronald D. Allen serves as the Canon for Global Missions for the Anglican Diocese of the Great Lakes within the Anglican Church in North America (ACNA). Through decades of faithful ministry, he has dedicated his life to evangelism, church planting, and global mission work.

sections.title: Ministry and Mission Work
sections.content: Since the beginning of his ordained ministry in Advent of 1965, Canon Dr. Allen, together with his wife Carolyn, has been instrumental in the planting of more than 120 churches. One of his most notable achievements was establishing the Heartland Parish in Fort Wayne, Indiana in 1985, which continues to serve as a vibrant center of ministry.

sections.title: Global Mission Involvement
items: Canon for Global Missions – Anglican Diocese of the Great Lakes (ACNA)
Contributor to the New Wineskins Global Missions movement
Consultant to numerous ministries and mission agencies
Advocate for global evangelism and church planting

sections.title: Role in Anglican Missions Africa
sections.content: As a member of the Board of Directors of Anglican Missions Africa, Canon Dr. Allen serves as an advisor and Custodian of AMA’s vision, providing valuable guidance to nurture a healthy and sustainable Church across Africa and beyond.
